title: This Robot Plays Chrome Dino Without Ever Losing 🦖
description:
The video demonstrates the operation of an automated system for autonomous gameplay of the "Chrome Dino" game utilizing an external photosensor and an Arduino microcontroller. Mounted on the laptop screen, the sensor detects incoming obstacles on the game track and triggers the character's automatic jump without human intervention - a fun piece of Arduino project engineering.

The technical principle of the system relies on optical contrast detection and hardware-level emulation of user input. An analog light-dependent resistor (LDR), attached with masking tape ahead of the character, continuously monitors the luminance level of the screen matrix. As the dark silhouette of an obstacle passes, an instantaneous drop in luminous flux occurs, which is registered by the Arduino Uno microcontroller via an analog input. In response to the signal variation, the microcontroller executes a predefined algorithm to transmit an impulse to a TowerPro MG90S servomotor or HID device emulator, generating a "Spacebar" keypress command.

This physical prototype serves as a clear illustration of the Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) concept and the implementation of direct-action closed-loop automatic control systems. The project demonstrates the practical application of foundational sensor technologies and microcontroller engineering for interacting with a digital environment through a physical layer, bypassing direct software modification of the application code - a great DIY robotics build.
